title: The apprentice tutor
scenario:
You help the trainer at a 40-person electrical firm. Six adult apprentices are studying for their trade exam in spring. The trainer wants to use AI in the course and asks you to check the plan first.

Use the exhibit. The firm, the plan and the people are made up for this case. Tool facts come from Gemini Apps Help, the ChatGPT docs and the Claude Help Center (October 2026).
exhibit:
TRAINER'S PLAN (made up)

  1. One shared project called "Exam tutor" for
     all six apprentices. Its instructions say:
     "Give the full worked answer at once, so
     they get through more questions."
  2. Weekly homework: 5 written questions.
     Last week all six hand-ins were perfect,
     and two were word for word the same.
  3. An apprentice asks: "How can I practise on
     my own at home, not just read answers?"
  4. Progress notes: the trainer wants to paste
     each apprentice's full name, test scores
     and sick days into a personal AI account
     to write the reports. The firm has no rule
     on this yet.

questions.prompt: Look at item 1. How should the trainer change the project instructions?

options.text: Keep them, because more answered questions means more learning
options.explanation: Reading more answers is not the same as learning. The Claude Help Center says the tool should not do the work learners are expected to do on their own.

options.text: Delete them, so the tool can decide by itself how to help each one
options.explanation: With no rules, the tool hands over the answer whenever it is asked. The teacher sets the rules.

options.text: Make the tool ask a question and give a hint before any solution
options.explanation: Right. Project instructions apply to every chat in the project, so the trainer can make the tool a tutor that lets apprentices try first.

options.text: Add "be friendly", but keep giving the full worked answer at once
options.explanation: A friendlier tone does not change the problem. The apprentices still get the answer before they think.

questions.prompt: Look at item 2. What is the best next step for the trainer?

options.text: Give all six full marks, since every answer in the hand-ins is right
options.explanation: Right answers on paper do not show who did the thinking. Two identical hand-ins are a warning sign.

options.text: Ask each apprentice to explain one answer in their own words, no tool
options.explanation: Right. The check is what the learner can do without the tool. If they can explain it, they learned it.

options.text: Ask the AI tool which of the hand-ins it wrote, and trust its reply
options.explanation: A tool's reply is not proof, and it says nothing about what each apprentice knows. The trainer checks the learners directly.

options.text: Make the homework longer, so it takes too long to copy from a tool
options.explanation: Longer homework is just as easy to paste. It does not show what each apprentice knows.

questions.prompt: Look at item 3. Which Gemini feature fits this apprentice best?

options.text: Guided Learning, or practice questions that come with hints
options.explanation: Right. Gemini Apps Help presents Gemini as a tutor, and says you can ask it for practice questions that give feedback and hints.

options.text: A full model answer for each homework question, ready to hand in
options.explanation: That is copying, not practice. The apprentice asked how to practise.

options.text: A summary of the course book, so there is less of it to read
options.explanation: A summary can help, but it is not practice. The apprentice wants to try questions.

options.text: Nothing, because Gemini's learning tools are only for teachers
options.explanation: Gemini Apps Help describes learning tools for the people who are learning, like quizzes with hints.

questions.prompt: Look at item 4. What should the trainer do?

options.text: Paste it all, since the reports are only for the firm's own use
options.explanation: Who reads the report later does not change where the data goes now. The firm has not decided this yet.

options.text: Paste it all, but delete the chat after the reports are written
options.explanation: Deleting later does not undo the choice to share it. The organisation decides first.

options.text: Use first names only, and keep the sick days and test scores in
options.explanation: First names with scores and sick days still point to real people in a small firm.

options.text: Leave out names and details until the firm sets its rule on this
options.explanation: Right. The Claude Help Center says the school or district's policy decides how identifiable learner data is used. Without that authorization, leave it out.
